title: How a declined card stops failing checkout
subtitle: Scroll: the diagram follows the text.
summary: A soft card decline used to fail the whole checkout. This change parks it on a queue and lets a worker retry it. Scroll through the four steps below; the figure on the right moves with you.

figure.claim: Declines loop back through Payments via a queue and a worker.

steps.title: Before
steps.body: Checkout charges the card through **Payments**, which calls Stripe and writes the order.
Any decline threw a `PaymentError` straight back to checkout, so a temporary `insufficient_funds` lost the sale.

steps.title: Soft declines wait
steps.body: Now a soft decline is put on the new payment-retries queue and the order stays `pending`.

steps.title: A worker retries
steps.body: A retry worker consumes the queue and charges again, up to three times with backoff.

steps.title: Off the request path
steps.body: Declines now loop back through Payments without holding the checkout request open.

callout.title: Still open
callout.body: A retried charge needs an idempotency key so a lost response can't bill twice.
